sections.title: ENTITY MATCHING TASK
sections.description: You are an expert at matching academic papers from DBLP and ACM databases. Your task is to find the candidate that refers to the same research paper as the left record.
unordered_list: Two papers match if they are the same research work, even if:
They have different formatting, punctuation, or capitalization
One title is slightly abbreviated or expanded
They use different notation (e.g., hyphens vs spaces, colons vs dashes)
Minor spelling variations or character encoding differences exist

sections.title: ACADEMIC PAPER MATCHING CRITERIA
sections.description: For academic papers, focus on these key matching signals:
ordered_list: Core title content: The main research topic should be identical
Key technical terms: Important domain-specific terminology should match
Paper structure: Similar length and complexity of titles often indicate same work
Author consistency: If author information exists, it should be compatible
Publication context: Same venue/year information should align if available

sections.title: COMMON ACADEMIC VARIATIONS TO ACCEPT
sections.description: These variations are NORMAL for the same paper across databases:
unordered_list: Subtitle differences: 'paper: a study' vs 'paper - a study' vs 'paper (a study)'
Abbreviation expansion: 'db systems' vs 'database systems'
Formatting changes: 'multi-dimensional' vs 'multidimensional'
Punctuation: extra/missing commas, periods, or spacing
Case variations: different capitalization patterns

sections.title: REASONING PROCESS
sections.description: Think step by step: Does this candidate represent the same research paper? Focus on core content similarity rather than exact string matching.

sections.title: RESPONSE FORMAT REQUIREMENTS
sections.description: Your response must follow this exact format:
unordered_list: You MUST respond with ONLY a single integer number
If the candidate matches the left record: respond with the candidate number
If the candidate does NOT match the left record: respond with "-1"
DO NOT include any words, explanations, or other text
DO NOT include quotes, brackets, or punctuation
Examples of CORRECT responses: 0 or -1
Examples of INCORRECT responses: "no match", "the paper title", "candidate 0"
